note: Generated; do not edit. Change the inputs and run `python scripts/site_facts.py`.

statuses.DEMONSTRATED: Measured on fresh or held-out data under a frozen protocol; the claim holds within the stated scope.
statuses.EXPERIMENTAL: Observed working live, but on very small samples (often n = 1) or constructed scenarios. A workflow demonstration, not a performance result.
statuses.NOT_YET_DEMONSTRATED: No study has shown it. Either none was run, or the studies run could not separate the arms.
statuses.NEGATIVE_RESULT: A study or qualification found the claim false or its gate missed. Kept visible on purpose.
statuses.INCONCLUSIVE: A study was run, but its differences are within noise: neither benefit nor harm is shown.
statuses.BLOCKED: Could not be run or qualified because of an external or safety blocker; the blocker is named.
statuses.UNSUPPORTED: Outside what repo-ai supports by design. Stated so nobody assumes otherwise.

entries.title: verify gives no false assurance on fresh held-out data
entries.result: 0 false assurances in 127 failing states; 0 new failures classified as pre-existing; 0 false alarms; runtime no-miss 96.7%.
entries.date_note: Session A qualification on build 903984a, completed before the RC1 freeze of 2026-10-27
entries.method: Held-out-7: frozen, independently labelled projects (pytest and node --test), run in podman containers on build 903984a.
entries.limits: Verdict CONDITIONAL_WITH_EXPLICIT_LIMITATIONS, for that build and container scope; not re-run on 0.9.0. unittest, TypeScript, Jest/Vitest and host sandboxes are not qualified on held-out data.

entries.title: Your working tree is never touched by a verify run
entries.result: Working tree unchanged in 234 of 234 runs; the integrity check also fails any run that touches it.
entries.method: Held-out-7, as above: the source tree is hashed before and after every run.
entries.limits: Containers only on held-out data; host sandboxes (seatbelt, bubblewrap) are covered by the test suite and CI sandbox jobs.

entries.limits: Label is stable candidate: no fresh preregistered validation of the whole command. Prose queries are weak (next entry).

entries.method: Session A's retrieval holdout, natural-language and error-message query classes.

entries.title: Live coding-agent candidates, independently re-verified
entries.result: Codex CLI 0.165.0 produced a PASS LIVE_CANDIDATE_VERIFIED change through repo-ai do, with coverage, apply (post-apply tests 4/4) and undo (bytes restored); agy 1.4.9 took part in the tournament and handoff journeys.
entries.sample_size: 1 workflow per journey per build (builds dfb6880, c505f74 and the freeze 9663ac3)
entries.method: Installed wheel in a clean venv on macOS seatbelt; synthetic projects written for the check; providers only through repo-ai do --run --allow-live-provider.
entries.limits: Synthetic tasks; the same author wrote task, tests and hidden oracle; costs UNKNOWN (subscriptions). IBM Bob produced live re-verified changes earlier (0.9.0.dev0 cycle) and was not re-run on 0.9.0.

entries.title: Hand unfinished work to a different agent
entries.result: Codex → agy: Codex left validated partial progress, the capsule verified VALID, agy kept Codex's diff byte-identical and reached PASS; independent hidden oracle 714/714. An earlier agy → Codex transfer also reached PASS.
entries.date_note: Codex → agy on 2026-10-29 (builds c505f74 and 9663ac3); agy → Codex earlier in October 2026
entries.method: Constructed scenario (stage A scoped to one file to force partial progress); live providers through repo-ai's mission path.
entries.limits: Constructed, n = 1; a handoff beating a restart is not shown.

entries.title: Tournaments abstain instead of picking a winner
entries.result: In abc-v3 both providers passed with different diffs on every task, so the no-tie-breaker rule abstained 4 of 4; on 2026-10-29 one live comparison abstained (distinct passing diffs) and one byte-identical pair was resolved by the equivalence rule.
entries.date_note: abc-v3 preregistered in the 0.9.0.dev2 cycle; launch journeys on 2026-10-29
entries.method: Codex + agy tournaments through repo-ai do --tournament; preregistered abc-v3 manifest.
entries.limits: A behaviourally different live tie was not exercised; that a tournament beats a single agent is not shown.

entries.title: Lift over a standalone coding agent
entries.result: In abc-v2 to v4 the bare provider already solved every task, so nothing could separate the arms; in abc-v1 the one-task difference of four is consistent with noise.
entries.date_note: abc-v1 to abc-v4 ran in the 0.9.0.dev0 to dev4 cycles
entries.sample_size: 4 studies, 14 tasks (4 + 4 + 4 + 2), one run per cell
entries.method: Preregistered manifests frozen before any live call; hidden graders outside the agent workspace; free controls (untouched FAIL, reference CORRECT, decoy FALSE_GREEN) per task.
entries.limits: Tasks, hidden tests and harness written by an AI agent; small synthetic tasks. Measuring lift needs tasks the bare provider fails at a non-trivial rate, at least 20 paired tasks and repeats.

entries.title: repo-ai reported PASS for a false green
entries.result: On node-slug, repo-ai reported PASS / LIVE_CANDIDATE_VERIFIED for a candidate that failed a hidden requirement the visible tests never stated.
entries.sample_size: 4 tasks, IBM Bob 2.0.9, one run per cell
entries.method: Preregistered abc-v1 with a hidden grader run in a separate copy.
entries.limits: This is the documented meaning of PASS (the visible checks passed), and this run is its counterexample.

entries.title: repo-ai catches false greens better than “tests pass”
entries.result: Calibration only: repo-ai (arm B) accepted 5 of 9 semantic decoys and 0 of 10 test-gaming controls, against 9 and 10 for “tests pass”; task-level discrimination 0 of 4. The confirmatory phase was not run.
entries.sample_size: 4 synthetic tasks, 29 candidates, no model calls
entries.method: Preregistered abc-v5 with a sealed grader, immutable manifests and exact power analysis; calibration run only.
entries.limits: One author wrote tasks, decoys and oracle. The thesis was narrowed to “names the requirements your tests do not pin, and resists test gaming” (DECISIONS L-007).

entries.title: Claude Code succeeds more often with repo-ai context
entries.result: Plain Claude 92%, repo-ai Core 90%, repo-ai Full 88%; Holm-adjusted p = 1.0 for every comparison; equivalence not shown either. Full cost about 10% more.
entries.method: Option A: preregistered, run blind; 25 tasks × 3 arms × 2 runs, Claude Sonnet.
entries.limits: Intervals about ±15 points: a gain or loss of 10–15 points is not ruled out. One clear harm with a known cause (guidance steered agents to lint instead of testing on one task).

entries.title: Core vs plain Claude on sealed-v2
entries.result: Plain solved 23 of 25 (92%), Core 21 of 25 (84%); −8 points, 95% CI −22 … +7, p = 0.5.
entries.method: Exploratory, as registered; sealed-v2 is no longer untouched.
entries.limits: Only 2 discordant tasks: the comparison carried almost no information.

entries.title: verify is faster than running the native suite
entries.result: On held-out-7, verify --run was slower than the native suite on 3 of 5 projects (1.44×, 1.70× and 2.31× the native time) and faster only on the two larger ones.
entries.date_note: held-out-7, before the RC1 freeze of 2026-10-27
entries.method: Wall-clock comparison inside the held-out-7 evaluation (podman containers).
entries.limits: Earlier, held-out-5 showed slower runs on 4 of 7 short suites (1.22–2.52×). On small suites the value is the classification, not time.

entries.title: Capability recommendation meets its recall gate
entries.result: FAIL: top-3 recall 0.385 against a gate of 0.80; shortlist recall@6 0.736; top-3 precision 0.712; 5 constraint-forbidden recommendations reached the top 3. Still above the lexical (0.088) and repository-only (0.286) baselines.
entries.method: Preregistered protocol frozen beforehand, measured once; tuning of the deterministic matcher stopped after three unsuccessful passes.
entries.limits: The raw results file sits in the private development history; the public record is docs/CAPABILITIES.md and docs/STATUS.md.

entries.title: Plugin inspection passes its fresh validation
entries.result: FAILED: 12 of 42 benign cases were blocked; executable-resolution coverage 0.25 (0.43 after a post-hoc corrective pass, still a fail). Nothing critical or unresolvable was reported eligible.
entries.method: Preregistered fresh validation of skills vet / inventory on plugin components.
entries.limits: Attack detection was not freshly validated (the synthetic attacks could not be produced). Since then a plugin is never reported eligible.

entries.title: Claude Code as an isolated execution provider
entries.result: Claude Code 2.1.312 failed authentication (“Not logged in”) inside repo-ai's scratch HOME, before any model call. It is supported as a host for context and hooks.
entries.method: Real run through repo-ai do on the freeze build; the provider's login is not a copyable file, and repo-ai does not work around that.
entries.limits: Blocked by the provider's authentication model, not by a repo-ai verdict. Update docs/engineering/evidence-matrix.json and site/src/data/providers.json together when this changes.

entries.title: The opt-in verify completion gate changes agent outcomes
entries.result: Its own tests pass; its effect on agent outcomes has never been measured.
entries.method: No study run.
entries.limits: Earlier recorded runs showed agents rarely call optional tools (0 skill invocations in 212 runs), which is why the gate exists.

entries.title: Windows, on fresh data
entries.result: Unit tests pass in CI (Python 3.10 and 3.13); no held-out or fresh-data run on Windows.
entries.method: CI unit tests only.
entries.limits: Windows has no host sandbox: verify --run needs --sandbox podman or docker.

entries.title: Missions (repo-ai do execution) on Windows
entries.result: Not supported: apply needs POSIX no-follow file operations.
entries.method: Design limit, stated in the platform matrix.
entries.limits: Index, context, impact and container-backed verify --run do work on Windows.

entries.title: Per-file test selection for Jest, Vitest and Mocha
entries.result: These runners are opaque to verify: they run only as a full suite, one runner per invocation; monorepos with several runners are not supported.
entries.method: Design limit.
entries.limits: pytest, unittest and node --test are split per file.
